scope: Corollary 2.7 (Active weight after cleaning) of the manuscript “The Kakeya maximal conjecture in three dimensions” (preprints/The-Kakeya-maximal-conjecture-in-three-dimensions-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 074 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 49cc52aa3de89f0e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 12. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let A be a finite collection of pairs (i, I), where I is a dyadic temporal block and the blocks assigned to each index i are disjoint. Let C be a partition of A. For a pair (i, I), its events are (i, J) with J ∈ Si ∩ I and have inherited weight ωi. Fix a ∈ R, ε ≥ 0, and 0 < ϑ0, σN ≤ 1. Suppose each pair has between Na−ε and Na+ε events. For C ∈ C put MC = X (i,I)∈C ωi. If a refinement retains at least a fraction ϑ0 of the event mass assigned to C, then its active weight in that cell satisfies X (i,I)∈C S′ i∩I̸=∅ ωi ≥ ϑ0N−2ε MC. Suppose further that each cell’s assigned events are partitioned into at most LN pieces, where LN ≥ 1 is an integer. Discard the pieces of mass less than σN /LN times their original cell’s event mass. This discards at most a fraction σN of the total event mass. If subsequent cleaning retains at least a fraction ϑ0 of each surviving piece’s original event mass, then the active weight on every occupied piece is at least ϑ0σN LN N−2ε MC. Here active weight counts each pair (i, I) meeting the piece once.
